target_customer: recreational and competitive runners, cyclists and triathletes who pay for coaching
problem: Generic training plans are rigid and do not adapt to real-life constraints or how the athlete's body is responding.
product_category: AI endurance-sports training coach (consumer health and fitness)

founders.name: Matin Tamizi
previous_startups: two fintech companies backed by a16z and Stripe, built and sold (names not listed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Created the most widely used open-source Garmin library, used by Stanford Health, per YC page. A YC launch post is written in the first person by a 41-year-old ultramarathoner but does not name the author, so age is not recorded.

competitors.name: Runna
competitors.what: personalised running training plans and coaching app
competitors.funding_then: about GBP 8M raised since 2021, including a GBP 5M round in 2023 led by JamJar, per press

competitors.name: Strava
competitors.what: activity tracking platform that added coaching through Runna

technical_complexity.rationale: Pulls wearable data (the founder authored an open-source Garmin library) and adapts training, recovery and nutrition daily; standard data integration plus LLM/model personalisation, with no research-grade element evident.

defensibility.rationale: No unique data or lock-in described; established apps (Runna, TrainingPeaks, Strava) already offer training plans, and the adaptive-coach concept is easy for them to replicate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Strava bought Runna (April 2025) and the YC-backed cycling app The Breakaway (May 2025) before Imperfect's batch, so incumbents were already buying this wedge.

market_need_then: Strava was seen as weak on training plans (press on Runna deal), and users' complaints about rigid plans appear in the founder's launch post; no user counts or revenue were reported for Imperfect.
outcome_analysis: Imperfect is a five-person YC Spring 2026 company building an adaptive AI coach for endurance athletes, led by a technical founder with prior fintech exits. It is too early for an outcome and no funding was found; the main risk is that Strava, after acquiring Runna and The Breakaway in 2025, and other established platforms already control the training-plan wedge.
notes: Very recent company; no funding information found (no data, not zero). Prior fintech companies are unnamed. Competitor sources are dated about a year before the batch rather than at it. YC launch post fetch could not confirm the author's identity.
